headline: Narayanganj: SI withdrawn after intoxicated video goes viral
summary: A Sub-Inspector of Police has been removed from his post following the spread of a video showing him in an intoxicated state.
details: A Sub-Inspector (SI) of Police has been withdrawn from his current posting in Narayanganj after a video of him in an intoxicated state went viral on social media.
The video, which spread rapidly across various platforms, showed the officer in a state of intoxication, leading to public outcry and administrative action.
Following the internal investigation into the conduct of the officer, the authorities decided to withdraw him from the city's police force.
The move comes as part of the police department's effort to maintain discipline and professional conduct among its personnel.

headline_marked: Police force [[women to reveal faces]] during hotel raid in Dhaka
headline: Police force women to reveal faces during hotel raid in Dhaka
summary: A leaked video shows DB police officers forcing detained women to uncover their faces, with some being threatened with violence.
details: A video has surfaced showing Detective Branch (DB) police forcing detained women to reveal their faces during a raid at the New Rongdhonu Residential Hotel in Abdullahpur, Dhaka, on August 12.

In the video, women are seen attempting to hide their faces with scarves and masks, while female police officers force them to uncover themselves. One woman is heard being told, 'Take it all off, don't cover it, or you'll be beaten.'

Police sources indicate that DC Elias Kabir of the DB Uttara Division ordered the officers to prevent the women from covering their faces. Kabir has denied the allegations, claiming the masks were removed for identification purposes and that no one was forced.

Human rights activists and lawyers have condemned the action as illegal and a violation of citizen rights. Former Human Rights Commission member Nur Khan stated that such behavior constitutes a form of pre-trial punishment.

Experts highlight that the Bangladesh Constitution and UN charters prohibit cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment. Furthermore, a 2012 High Court directive explicitly instructed law enforcement to avoid presenting detainees in front of the media.
The report also reveals a trend of police collaborating with YouTubers and content creators to film raids for 'views' and profit, a practice criticized by academics as unethical and illegal.
